author: NorthEast News Desk
body: New Hampshire’s new protections for cryptocurrency ATM customers are scheduled to take effect Dec. 16, giving residents additional safeguards as officials try to curb scams that direct people to send money through kiosks.

The law limits a customer’s cryptocurrency ATM transactions to $2,000 per day. For a customer’s first transaction, the operator must hold the transaction for at least 48 hours, during which the customer can cancel it and receive a refund.

Operators also must display fraud warnings, disclose fees and exchange-rate spreads, provide receipts and use prompts or other measures designed to identify suspicious transactions. A customer seeking a fraud refund generally must contact the operator and law enforcement within 14 days.

The rules do not make every cryptocurrency payment reversible, but they create a defined process for transactions made through covered kiosks. The changes follow warnings about impersonation and other scams in which victims are told to convert cash into cryptocurrency and transfer it immediately.
dek: New Hampshire’s new cryptocurrency ATM rules will add transaction limits, a first-use delay and a fraud-refund process beginning Dec. 16.
headline: New Hampshire crypto ATM protections set to take effect in December
